summary: Table Bluff Light, a wooden tower on a bluff south of Humboldt Bay, first lit 31 October 1892, automated 1953; its tower moved to Eureka's marina in 1987.

light.characteristic: fixed white (1892); revolving lens flashing every five seconds from 1911 (LH; Bulletin 1912)
light.discontinued_note: USLHS gives 1961; LH and Point Cabrillo say active until 1971.

lens.where: Humboldt Bay Maritime Museum, Samoa (lens retrieved from Old Point Loma)

structures.note: Dwelling and duplex demolished after WWII (LH); tower cut in two and moved to Woodley Island Marina, Eureka, in 1987.

access.note: USLHS: not open to the public. The bluff's views are open to visitors (LH).

visit.note: Lighthouse Friends says visitors can enjoy the views; all historic structures were demolished by 2012 (BLM).

facts.agency: Bureau of Land Management (bluff site, per LH)

events.note: Board recommends relocating the light to Table Bluff (LH).
Inspector and engineer select the Table Bluff site; Board report dates the visit 8 May 1891 (LH says 1892).
Tower and keeper's dwelling contract to W. M. Wickersham, $16,949; bids opened 21 March 1892.
Fourth-order fixed Fresnel lens first exhibited from the new station, 31 October 1892.
Brick foundation built under a 50,000-gallon water tank.
Revolving lens; flashes every five seconds (LH). Bulletin 1912 lists the change to flashing, with an incandescent oil-vapor illuminant.
Two earthquake shocks, 31 January 1922, about 5:15 a.m.; light put out, mantle broken; keeper on watch.
Severe shocks, 22 January 1923; light put out at about 1:05 a.m., mantle broken; no other damage.
Electricity; fog signal changed from a siren to a type F diaphone (LH).
One of the first automated; modern optic installed; fog signal discontinued; Fresnel lens to Old Point Loma.
USLHS 'Year Discontinued: 1961'. LH and Point Cabrillo say 1971.
Bought by a Christian youth ministry and renamed Lighthouse Ranch (LH).
Deactivated after a new light was established at the entrance to Humboldt Harbor (LH); 'active until 1971' (Point Cabrillo).
Jim Durkin buys the ranch; a commune forms there (LH).
Tower cut in two and moved to Eureka's Woodley Island Marina.
Gospel Outreach sells the land to the state for $1.5 million (LH).
BLM contract for demolition of remaining structures, $307,125 (LH); Point Cabrillo: BLM demolished the buildings in 2012.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board's report for 1891 dates the inspector and engineer's visit to 8 May 1891. LH gives 1892. The Board's report is the primary record, so 1891 is used.
LH dates the revolving lens to 1911. The Bulletin's 1912 listing of Table Bluff among lights changed from fixed to flashing describes the same change.

notes_for_editor: End date disputed: USLHS 1961 (its Year Discontinued field); LH and Point Cabrillo 1971; Wikipedia infobox 1971 with text 1975 (lead only, not cited); Lighthouse Digest search snippet gives 1972 (not read, not cited). The land price: the Board's 1892 report prints a figure the OCR reads as 82,220 (scan p. 565); the page image reads $2,226, matching LH. The Board's 1891 visit date (8 May 1891) differs from LH's 1892. Printed page numbers for the 1893 entry (166-167) are unconfirmed, so the report is cited by scan page. The 1922 keeper-on-watch time (5:20 a.m.) is read from OCR that is partly garbled. The Pozanac tremor is from LH only and undated. Keeper roster lines are the USLHS record as printed (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory); not checked against primary registers. Chronicling America searches for Table Bluff with lighthouse terms (CA, 1892-1900) gave no relevant pages; no newspaper is cited. Ray Glavich is named as LH names him, a volunteer role after 1960; no personal details beyond the role. BLM ownership and the 2012 demolition rest on LH and Point Cabrillo; the BLM's own page was not read. The Wikipedia managing-agent claim (Humboldt Bay Harbor District) is unverified and not used. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1892 land price is $2,226 on the page image (the OCR's 82,220 is an error), so the story gives $2,226 from the report and LH; the contract for the buildings reads $16,949 on the image (printed p. 187; the OCR says $16,049), and the story attributes the $16,949 and the Wickersham name to LH. The distance from the old station is 'about 4 miles south of the present light' in the 1891 report and 'about 5 miles S. by W.' in the 1893 list of station moves; the story states both and does not reconcile them. The 1922 time (5.20 a.m.) is from the bulletin's OCR, which reads 'had light in operation It t 5.20 a. m.'; the bulletin PDF could not be viewed in the browser (the site returned a file download, which was not retried), so the time is stated without 'about'.
